claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain at least five metals in equal or near-equal atomic percentages, which increases the configurational entropy of the disordered solid solution.
The nanoparticles begin as a uniform, single-phase solid solution.
High configurational entropy can dominate temperature-activated diffusion and maintain a single-phase nanoparticle solid solution from 473 to 1923 K.
Maintenance of the solid solution requires constituent metals with comparable bond strengths and diffusion barriers.
Slight compositional deviations can promote atomic segregation and phase transformation.
Small local bond-strength differences can promote atomic segregation and phase transformation.
Controlled heating over 473–1923 K allows temperature-dependent structural and chemical stability to be compared between equiatomic and perturbed nanoparticles.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation from interfering with the intrinsic stability assessment.
Heating rates must be slow enough to allow atomic diffusion.
Differential local bond strengths and atomic diffusion barriers are the structural mediator of stability.
At moderate temperatures, configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution against minor atomic rearrangements.
At higher temperatures, increased atomic mobility can cause diffusion-driven segregation when local bonding differences outweigh configurational-entropy stabilization.
The combined effects of composition and temperature govern phase stability and the scale of decomposition.
Strictly equiatomic nanoparticles with similar diffusion barriers will retain unchanged lattice parameters and uniform elemental distributions throughout 473–1923 K.
Nanoparticles with slight compositional deviations will develop secondary phases or chemical inhomogeneity during heating.
Nanoparticles with more varied constituent bond strengths will develop secondary phases or chemical inhomogeneity during heating.
Particle size and heating rate must permit intrinsic diffusion effects to be observed without extrinsic confounding.
The temperature and perturbation thresholds that trigger segregation are not specified.
The hypothesis is falsified if equiatomic nanoparticles segregate to an extent similar to or greater than compositionally deviated samples under identical thermal conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism attribute stability to an interplay among configurational entropy, bond strengths, and diffusion barriers, whereas the falsification rule characterizes the proposition as one in which high configurational entropy alone governs stability.
